newsitem.title: UK: Police tackle big suspected bomb in N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Police tackle big suspected bomb in N.Ireland.

text.p: Army bomb disposal experts on Monday examined a huge Irish Republican Army (IRA) bomb which the guerrillas abandoned in a residential area of a Northern Irish town on the first anniversary of their broken 17-month ceasefire.
"We are working on a device the IRA claim to have abandoned in the area. They said it was a 1,000-pound bomb," a spokesman for the Royal Ulster Constabulary said.
Police said the device could have killed many people and caused huge damage had it been detonated.
It was dumped close to a hotel with 250 guests and a housing estate at Strabane, some 50 miles (80 km) northwest of Belfast.
The IRA, which is fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland, telephoned police to say it had abandoned the device on a building site.
Security sources believe they wanted to detonate it at a British security target or government building but were thwarted by security patrols and decided to abandon the device.
It was left on February 9, the first anniversary of an IRA bomb attack at London's Canary Wharf business complex which marked the end of the guerrillas' cesefire.
The IRA says its political wing, Sinn Fein, should be invited to Belfast peace talks but Britain says only an unequivocal and permanent truce will give it a place at the talks.
